threads.body: This moves the instrumentation's `library(...)` compile/test dependency from the supported floor (3.0.0) to 3.5.0 while the Ktor 3 module still targets the whole 3.x line. The build conventions document that `library(old)` is used to keep instrumentation compiling against the old API while latest-dependency overrides exercise newer versions (`conventions/src/main/kotlin/io.opentelemetry.instrumentation.base.gradle.kts:13-21,173-177`). Keeping this at 3.0.0 and adding a 3.5-specific test/runtime override would avoid accidentally relying on APIs unavailable to 3.0.x users.

This updates the javaagent module's `library(...)` dependency to 3.5.0, but the muzzle range above still advertises support for Ktor `[3.0.0,)`. The build conventions use the `library(...)` version as the compile baseline so the instrumentation does not accidentally reference newer APIs (`conventions/src/main/kotlin/io.opentelemetry.instrumentation.base.gradle.kts:13-21,173-177`). Please keep the compile baseline at 3.0.0 or narrow the supported range if 3.5.0 is now required.

Because this testing project is pulled into the Ktor 3 library/javaagent tests, raising its Ktor dependencies to 3.5.0 makes the regular test runtime resolve to 3.5.0 even if the instrumentation compile baseline stays at 3.0.0. That removes coverage for the supported 3.0.x floor; use a dedicated 3.5-specific test configuration instead of upgrading the shared testing module.

If this regression test times out or the request throws, the `client.close()` below is skipped, leaving the CIO client/threads running after a failed test. Ensure the client is closed from cleanup (for example via a `finally`) so failures do not leak resources and mask the original timeout.

This issue also appears on line 73 of the same file.

[Testing] This uses Kotlin's `assert`, which is disabled unless the test JVM is started with assertions enabled. The repository's Gradle test configuration does not enable `-ea`, so this span-duration check can silently be skipped; use an always-on test assertion instead.

[Testing] This chooses an available port and closes the socket before Netty binds it, leaving a race where another process can claim the port and make the test fail intermittently. Prefer binding the embedded server to port 0 and reading the assigned connector port, or using the existing HTTP test server utilities that own the port reservation.

threads.body: `latestDepTestLibrary` dependencies are using the unbounded dynamic version `+`, which can pull in a future incompatible major (or a non-release) and make latest-deps CI flaky. Elsewhere in the repo these are typically constrained to the supported major line (e.g., `2.+` in `instrumentation/ktor/ktor-2.0/*`). Consider changing these to `3.+` (or another bounded range consistent with the intended support window).
